note: Wider browser-games library. Every destination is a real, independently verifiable project. Clean-room / decompilation builds point to the host where they actually run. Each entry carries game-specific copy: what the original is, what this build needs, and how to open it.

games.name: Minecraft Classic
games.summary: Mojang's own free browser build of the original creative-mode Minecraft.
games.whatItIs: The official browser edition of Minecraft Classic, published by Mojang and free to play with no account. It is the original creative mode only, so there is no survival, no mobs and no crafting. Multiplayer worlds are peer-to-peer: they exist only while the person hosting keeps the tab open, which is why the player list is usually tiny.
howToOpen: Open the official Classic page at classic.minecraft.net.
Enter a nickname when prompted, or leave it blank.
Click the canvas to lock the pointer, then pick a block from the hotbar.
games.statusNote: Official Mojang build. Creative mode only, and multiplayer worlds vanish when the host closes the tab.

games.name: Eaglercraft
games.summary: A community-built Minecraft client that runs entirely in a browser tab.
games.whatItIs: Eaglercraft is a long-running community project that reimplements a Minecraft client so it runs inside a single browser page, including a form of multiplayer. It has existed for years and is packaged as one page rather than an install. It is a fan client with its own quirks and bugs, and it is not affiliated with Mojang or Microsoft.
whatYouNeed: A stable connection if you want to join community servers
Acceptance that this is a fan client, not an official release
howToOpen: Open the Eaglercraft play page.
Choose a version from the list, then start a single-player world or open the server list.
Read the project's own notes for controls and server rules.
games.statusNote: Community client with its own bugs and version quirks. Not affiliated with Mojang or Microsoft.

games.name: Prince of Persia
games.summary: The 1989 dungeon classic, reimplemented in HTML5 and playable instantly.
games.whatItIs: PrinceJS is a reimplementation of the 1989 MS-DOS Prince of Persia in HTML5 and JavaScript. The original level design, the deliberately slow animation timing and the sword duels are recreated, so it still demands the same patience the original did. It starts straight in the tab with no download.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard for the arrow keys and the action key
howToOpen: Open PrinceJS.
Read the on-screen key list first, because the controls are not the modern default.
Start a new game and take the first jumps slowly.
games.statusNote: Reimplementation of the 1989 MS-DOS original, playable directly in the browser.

games.name: Super Mario 64 (sm64js)
games.altName: Native JavaScript port of Super Mario 64
games.summary: A JavaScript WebGL port of Super Mario 64 built from the decompilation.
games.whatItIs: sm64js is a native JavaScript port of Super Mario 64 derived from the community decompilation of the N64 original. It renders through WebGL and keeps the castle hub and the star-collecting structure. Because it is a native port rather than an emulator, performance depends on your browser rather than on emulating N64 hardware.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard or a USB gamepad
Patience while the assets download on the first load
howToOpen: Open the sm64js build.
Wait for the asset loader to finish before touching the controls.
Check the project page for the button layout, which is not the N64 original's.
games.statusNote: Community port built from the Super Mario 64 decompilation. Not affiliated with Nintendo.

games.name: Doom (1993)
games.altName: id Software's Doom, DOS build in browser
games.summary: The original Doom running from a real DOS executable inside the browser.
games.whatItIs: This entry runs the original 1993 Doom through a browser-based DOS environment rather than a JavaScript rewrite, so the genuine executable and its behaviour are preserved. That means the original renderer and sound handling, with the keyboard-only defaults of the era and mouse look added by the emulation layer.
whatYouNeed: Virtual touch controls if you are on a phone
howToOpen: Open the Doom page on DOS Zone.
Click the screen to capture input.
Press Escape for the in-game menu and key bindings.
games.statusNote: Runs the genuine 1993 DOS executable through browser-based emulation, not a rewrite.

games.name: The Ultimate Doom
games.altName: Doom with the fourth episode, in browser
games.summary: The expanded 1995 retail release, including the fourth episode.
games.whatItIs: The Ultimate Doom is the 1995 retail release that added a fourth episode, Thy Flesh Consumed, to the original three. It runs here through the same browser DOS environment as the 1993 build, so the difference between the two entries is the content, not the engine. Episode four is noticeably harder than the original campaign.
whatYouNeed: Familiarity with classic Doom controls, since there is no tutorial
howToOpen: Open the Ultimate Doom page.
Click to capture the mouse.
Pick an episode from the menu; episode four is the hardest of the four.
games.statusNote: Runs the 1995 retail release, including the fourth episode, through browser-based DOS emulation.

games.name: Doom & Fan Mods
games.summary: Classic Doom alongside community conversions and themed total conversions.
games.whatItIs: A fan-run browser Doom collection that bundles classic Doom with community conversions and themed total conversions built on the same engine. Because the mods vary widely in scope and quality, it is best treated as a launcher to browse than as one curated game. It is a fan collection, not an official release.
whatYouNeed: A willingness to experiment, since mod quality varies
howToOpen: Open the collection.
Pick a build from the list and note which base game it expects.
Click the canvas to capture input, then check the in-game key bindings.
games.statusNote: Fan-run collection bundling classic Doom with community conversions. Not an official release.

games.name: Duke Nukem 3D
games.summary: The 1996 shooter running from its DOS build in the browser.
games.whatItIs: Duke Nukem 3D runs here from the 1996 DOS build through browser-based emulation, so the interactive scenery, the weapon set and the level design behave as they did on period hardware. It was one of the first shooters to build a genuinely city-like environment rather than corridors, and the build is the original one rather than a remake. The page is free to play without registration.
whatYouNeed: A click on the canvas to capture input
howToOpen: Open the Duke Nukem 3D page on DOS Zone.
Let the DOS bundle finish loading, then click the screen to capture input.
Use the in-game menu for controls, sound and difficulty.
games.statusNote: Runs the 1996 DOS build through browser emulation. Free to play without registration.

games.name: Wolfenstein 3D
games.summary: The original 1992 first-person shooter, running in a browser tab.
games.whatItIs: Wolfenstein 3D is the 1992 shooter that established the first-person genre, built on the engine family that Doom would later extend. This entry runs the DOS build through browser emulation with no installation, and the level layouts are the original ones rather than a modern remake. There is no mouse look, so expect the period control scheme.
whatYouNeed: A click on the canvas to capture input
howToOpen: Open the Wolfenstein 3D page on DOS Zone.
Wait for the DOS bundle to load, then click the screen to begin.
Use the in-game menu to set difficulty and controls before the first level.
games.statusNote: Runs the original 1992 DOS build through browser emulation. Free to play without registration.

games.name: Command & Conquer: Red Alert
games.summary: The 1996 real-time strategy classic, with browser multiplayer support.
games.whatItIs: Red Alert runs here through a browser DOS environment that also offers a multiplayer lobby. You can skirmish against the computer or join a browser match, and the original 1996 balance and unit roster are preserved because it is the real DOS build rather than a remake. Real-time strategy is unplayable without a mouse, so this is not a touch-friendly entry.
whatYouNeed: A mouse, which real-time strategy genuinely requires
A stable connection if you join multiplayer
howToOpen: Open the Red Alert multiplayer page.
Create or join a lobby.
Read the in-game controls before the first match starts.
games.statusNote: Browser DOS build of the 1996 release, with a working multiplayer lobby.

games.name: Red Alert 2: Chrono Divide
games.summary: A fan project that recreates Red Alert 2 for the browser.
games.whatItIs: Chrono Divide is a fan project that recreates Red Alert 2 for the browser. It is an independent build rather than an official release, and it targets the classic skirmish and multiplayer experience rather than the campaign. Expect the familiar factions and units behind a browser-native interface, with the project's own balance decisions.
howToOpen: Open the Chrono Divide site.
Create an account or start a skirmish, depending on what the project currently offers.
Read the project's own notes for controls and game modes.
games.statusNote: Fan-made recreation of Red Alert 2. Independent project, not an official release.

games.name: OpenTTD
games.summary: The open-source Transport Tycoon Deluxe, running in the browser.
games.whatItIs: OpenTTD is the long-running open-source reimplementation of Transport Tycoon Deluxe, and both its engine and its graphics are free. That makes this browser build a complete game rather than a demo, and it supports importing and exporting save games, so a company you have spent hours building is not lost when you close the tab.
whatYouNeed: Patience for the first asset load, which is the slowest part
howToOpen: Open the browser build.
Wait for the graphics to load.
Start a new game and follow the in-game tutorial before building a network.
games.statusNote: Open-source engine with free graphics, and save import and export is supported.

games.name: OpenRCT2
games.summary: The open-source RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 engine, running in a browser tab.
games.whatItIs: OpenRCT2 is an open-source reimplementation of RollerCoaster Tycoon 2. The engine is free, but it deliberately does not ship the original art and sound, so you must supply the data files from a copy you own. That makes it the one entry in this library that genuinely requires a purchase before it will run.
whatYouNeed: A legally owned copy of RollerCoaster Tycoon 2
A desktop browser with enough local storage for the data files
The project's own instructions for uploading game data
howToOpen: Read the site's notes on which game files are required.
Upload data from a copy you own.
Start a scenario once the assets are loaded.
games.statusNote: The engine is open source but expects original RollerCoaster Tycoon 2 data that you supply yourself.

games.name: GoldenEye 007
games.summary: The N64 split-screen shooter legend, rebuilt to run in a browser.
games.whatItIs: GoldenEye 007 is Rare's 1997 N64 shooter, built around the 1995 film and known for its four-player split-screen multiplayer and its stealth-or-firefight mission design. This browser build runs from the community decompilation rather than a ROM emulator, so it is the reconstructed engine rather than a dumped cartridge, and the default controls are the project's own.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard and mouse, or a gamepad
A modern browser, since the build targets current WebGL features
howToOpen: Open the GoldenEye 007 build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader to finish.
Check the control scheme before a mission, as the default binds are not the N64 layout.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 original, hosted by Decomp Games. Not affiliated with the original publishers.

games.name: Perfect Dark
games.summary: Rare's N64 shooter, rebuilt from the decompilation to run in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Perfect Dark is Rare's 2000 N64 follow-up to GoldenEye, a sci-fi shooter starring Joanna Dark. It shipped with a Combat Simulator that supported bots, co-operative missions and a counter-operative mode, which was unusually complete for a console shooter of the era. This build runs from the community decompilation of the N64 original.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard and mouse or a gamepad
Patience for the initial load, which pulls down the level assets
howToOpen: Open the Perfect Dark build on Decomp Games.
Let the loader complete.
Read the control notes, then try the Combat Simulator with bots before the campaign.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 original, hosted by Decomp Games. Includes the Combat Simulator with bots.

games.name: Doom 64
games.summary: The darker N64 Doom, rebuilt to run in a browser tab.
games.whatItIs: Doom 64 is the 1997 N64 entry, and it is not a port of the PC games: it has its own levels, its own darker lighting and a redesigned weapon set. That makes it worth playing even if you already know the PC Doom titles well. This build runs from the community decompilation of the N64 original.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard and mouse or a gamepad
A modern browser with WebGL support
howToOpen: Open the Doom 64 build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Check the in-game options for controls and brightness, since the original is deliberately dark.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64-exclusive original, hosted by Decomp Games. Not a port of the PC Doom.

games.name: Star Fox 64
games.summary: The on-rails space shooter, rebuilt to run in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Star Fox 64 is the 1997 N64 rail shooter, a reimagining of the SNES original with voiced characters and branching routes. You fly along a set path rather than exploring freely, and the route you take determines which ending you reach. This build runs from the community decompilation of the N64 original.
whatYouNeed: A modern browser that supports WebGL
howToOpen: Open the Star Fox 64 build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader to finish.
Check the controls, then pick a route from the map screen.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 rail shooter, hosted by Decomp Games. Branching routes are intact.

games.name: Duke Nukem: Zero Hour
games.summary: The N64 Duke Nukem outing, rebuilt to run in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Duke Nukem: Zero Hour is the 1999 N64 outing, and it differs sharply from the PC Duke games: it is a third-person shooter with a time-travel plot that moves between eras. This build runs from the community decompilation of the N64 version, so it is not the DOS Duke Nukem 3D that most people mean by the name.
whatYouNeed: A gamepad or keyboard and mouse
howToOpen: Open the Zero Hour build on Decomp Games.
Let the loader finish.
Read the control notes before starting, since the third-person camera takes adjusting.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 title, hosted by Decomp Games. Distinct from the DOS Duke Nukem 3D.

games.name: Freedoom
games.altName: Free Doom-engine game with original assets
games.summary: A completely free Doom-engine game with its own art and levels.
games.whatItIs: Freedoom is a free, open-source game built on the Doom engine with entirely original art, sound and levels, so nothing is borrowed from the commercial release. That makes it the cleanest way to play a Doom-style game in a browser, and it remains compatible with the same source ports as the original. It ships as two replacement episodes for the classic campaigns.
whatYouNeed: Nothing else, since every asset is free and included
howToOpen: Open the Freedoom build on Decomp Games.
Click the canvas to capture input.
Check the in-game menu for controls, then choose a difficulty.
games.statusNote: Free and open-source assets throughout, hosted by Decomp Games. No commercial files required.

games.name: OpenTyrian
games.summary: A free, open-source vertical shooter with a full campaign.
games.whatItIs: OpenTyrian is an open-source reimplementation of Tyrian, the 1995 vertical scrolling shooter by Epic MegaGames. It keeps the full campaign and the ship-upgrade progression, and it ships with free assets rather than the original commercial ones. The result is a complete shooter rather than a demo level.
whatYouNeed: Nothing else, since the assets are free and included
howToOpen: Open the OpenTyrian build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Pick a difficulty and start the campaign, then spend upgrade points between levels.
games.statusNote: Open-source reimplementation of Tyrian with free assets, hosted by Decomp Games. Full campaign included.

games.name: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
games.summary: The N64 adventure classic, running in a browser from the decompilation.
games.whatItIs: Ocarina of Time is Nintendo's 1998 N64 adventure, and it is the game that established lock-on targeting, context-sensitive buttons and the 3D action-adventure template that followed it. This build runs from the Ship of Harkinian decompilation with a WebGL2 renderer, and its initial load is one of the larger ones in this library. It is a fan project and is not affiliated with Nintendo.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard and mouse or a gamepad
Patience for the initial load, which is one of the larger ones here
howToOpen: Open the Ocarina of Time build on Decomp Games.
Let the loader finish before touching the controls.
Check the control scheme before leaving the first area, as the binds are remappable.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build from the Ship of Harkinian decompilation. Not affiliated with Nintendo.

games.name: Mario Kart 64
games.summary: The N64 kart racer, rebuilt to run in a browser tab.
games.whatItIs: Mario Kart 64 is Nintendo's 1997 N64 kart racer, and it is the entry that made four-player split-screen racing a standard. It includes the Grand Prix cups and the battle mode, and its item set still defines the series. This build runs from the community decompilation of the N64 original.
whatYouNeed: A gamepad is strongly recommended for steering
howToOpen: Open the Mario Kart 64 build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Read the control notes, then pick a cup or a battle arena.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 kart racer, hosted by Decomp Games. Not affiliated with Nintendo.

games.name: F-Zero X
games.summary: The fast, futuristic N64 racer, rebuilt for the browser.
games.whatItIs: F-Zero X is Nintendo's 1998 anti-gravity racer, and it is unusual for running 30 machines on track at once at a locked frame rate. It also includes the X Cup, which generates its tracks randomly, and a Death Race mode with no track at all. This build runs from the community decompilation of the N64 original.
whatYouNeed: A gamepad or keyboard, since precise steering matters
howToOpen: Open the F-Zero X build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Check the controls, then start a cup or try the randomly generated X Cup.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 racer, hosted by Decomp Games. Includes the randomly generated X Cup.

games.name: Diddy Kong Racing
games.summary: The N64 adventure racer with cars, planes and hovercraft.
games.whatItIs: Diddy Kong Racing is Rare's 1997 N64 racer, and it mixes racing with a single-player adventure that has an explorable overworld and boss races. It also uses three vehicle types, cars, planes and hovercraft, which the courses switch between mid-race. This build runs from the community decompilation of the N64 original.
whatYouNeed: A modern browser, plus time for the overworld to load
howToOpen: Open the Diddy Kong Racing build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Check the control notes, then start the adventure mode rather than a single race.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 adventure racer, hosted by Decomp Games. Three vehicle types included.

games.name: Super Smash Bros.
games.summary: The original N64 party fighter, rebuilt for the browser.
games.whatItIs: Super Smash Bros. is HAL Laboratory's 1999 N64 platform fighter, the first in the series. It replaces health bars with an accumulating damage percentage, and it shipped with twelve characters and support for four players at once. This build runs from the community decompilation of the N64 original.
whatYouNeed: Gamepads for two-player or four-player matches
howToOpen: Open the Super Smash Bros. build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Check the control scheme, then pick a mode and characters before the match.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the original N64 fighter, hosted by Decomp Games. Not affiliated with Nintendo.

games.name: Banjo-Kazooie
games.summary: The N64 collect-a-thon platformer, rebuilt for the browser.
games.whatItIs: Banjo-Kazooie is Rare's 1998 N64 platformer, built around exploration and collection: Jiggies open new worlds and musical Notes gate your progress. The bear-and-bird pairing gives it a move set that expands as you learn new abilities, so later worlds depend on earlier ones. This build runs from the community decompilation of the N64 original.
whatYouNeed: A modern browser, and the patience for a collect-a-thon
howToOpen: Open the Banjo-Kazooie build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Check the controls before leaving the first world, since the move list grows as you play.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 collect-a-thon, hosted by Decomp Games.

games.name: Conker's Bad Fur Day
games.summary: Rare's mature N64 platformer, rebuilt to run in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Conker's Bad Fur Day is Rare's 2001 N64 platformer, and it is aimed squarely at adults: the humour is crude and the level design parodies films and other games. It also includes several distinct multiplayer modes alongside the campaign. This build runs from the community decompilation of the N64 original and carries the same mature content.
whatYouNeed: An audience that is old enough for the content
howToOpen: Open the Conker build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Check the controls before starting; the multiplayer modes are separate from the campaign.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 title, hosted by Decomp Games. Contains mature content.

games.name: Sonic the Hedgehog 2
games.summary: The Mega Drive speed platformer, rebuilt to run in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Sonic the Hedgehog 2 is the 1992 Mega Drive sequel that introduced the Spin Dash and Tails as a companion. It also added a split-screen two-player versus mode, which the first game did not have. This build runs from the community decompilation of the Mega Drive original rather than a ROM emulator.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard or gamepad for the Spin Dash timing
howToOpen: Open the Sonic 2 build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Check the controls, then pick a zone or start the two-player versus mode.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the 1992 Mega Drive original, hosted by Decomp Games.

games.name: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night
games.summary: The PlayStation action classic, rebuilt to run in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night is Konami's 1997 PlayStation title, and it is the game that gave the exploration-focused action format its name by mixing a large map with RPG levelling and equipment. It also hides a second, inverted castle behind the first ending. This build runs from the community decompilation of the PlayStation original.
whatYouNeed: A gamepad is recommended for the combat timing
howToOpen: Open the Symphony of the Night build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Check the controls before you start exploring the castle, since the map is large.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the 1997 PlayStation original, hosted by Decomp Games.

games.name: Super Metroid
games.summary: The SNES exploration classic, rebuilt to run in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Super Metroid is Nintendo's 1994 SNES title, and it set the template for exploration-driven action adventures: an interconnected map, abilities that unlock new routes and a largely wordless story. It is also famous for rewarding sequence-breaking, so skilled players can reach areas out of order. This build runs from the community decompilation of the SNES original.
whatYouNeed: A modern browser, plus the map screen button noted
howToOpen: Open the Super Metroid build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Check the controls before you leave the first area, and note the map screen button.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the 1994 SNES original, hosted by Decomp Games.

games.name: Beneath a Steel Sky
games.summary: The cyberpunk point-and-click adventure, free to play in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Beneath a Steel Sky is Revolution Software's 1994 cyberpunk point-and-click adventure, set in a future Australia and following Robert Foster and his robot companion Joey. Its publisher released it as freeware in 2003, which is why it can be played legally at no cost. It runs here through a browser build of the original.
whatYouNeed: Patience with adventure-game puzzles, which do not hold your hand
howToOpen: Open the Beneath a Steel Sky build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Use the in-game menu for controls and saving, and save often.
games.statusNote: Released as freeware by the publisher in 2003. Browser build hosted by Decomp Games.

games.name: Open Cadet
games.summary: An open-source arcade game with free assets, playable in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Open Cadet is a smaller open-source arcade title distributed with its own free assets, so nothing has to be supplied by the player. It is one of the lighter entries in this library and is included for completeness rather than as a headline title, so treat it as a short arcade diversion rather than a long campaign.
whatYouNeed: Nothing else, since the assets are free and included
howToOpen: Open the Open Cadet build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the loader.
Check the controls on the title screen before starting.
games.statusNote: Smaller open-source arcade title with free assets, hosted by Decomp Games.

games.name: Craft
games.summary: A minimal open-source voxel sandbox you can play in a tab.
games.whatItIs: Craft is a minimal open-source voxel sandbox, a stripped-down take on block building built on a very small codebase. It has no survival layer, no mobs and no crafting tree, so it is closer to a building toy than to a full game. All of its assets are free and included.
whatYouNeed: Nothing else, since the assets are free and included
howToOpen: Open the Craft build on Decomp Games.
Wait for the world to generate.
Check the controls for movement and placing blocks, since there is no tutorial.
games.statusNote: Minimal open-source voxel sandbox with free assets, hosted by Decomp Games. No survival or crafting.

games.name: Wave Race 64
games.summary: The N64 jet-ski racer, rebuilt to run in a browser from the clean-room pipeline.
games.whatItIs: Wave Race 64 is Nintendo's 1996 N64 jet-ski racer, and its selling point was water that behaved like water: the surface rises and falls, and you have to read the swell to hold a racing line. This build runs the retail program through EmulatorJS with textures, images and audio regenerated by the clean-room pipeline, so it ships no original ROM, textures or audio. The regenerated art deliberately differs from the retail release, and the announcer is a placeholder synthetic voice.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard or a standard gamepad, detected automatically
Acceptance that regenerated assets differ from the retail release
howToOpen: Open the Wave Race 64 build on Decomp Games.
Tap or press a key once, since sound only starts after your first input.
Pick a championship from the menu; touch controls are still being rolled out, so use a keyboard or pad.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 original, hosted by Decomp Games. Boots and starts a race; assets are regenerated, not retail.

games.name: Open Skyways
games.summary: An arcade racer where you steer and jump a craft along narrow sky roads.
games.whatItIs: Open Skyways rebuilds the engine behind SkyRoads, the 1993 arcade racer in which you steer a craft along narrow elevated roads and jump the gaps before you run out of road. It pairs that engine with thirty independently authored courses and replacement menus, dashboard and graphics, so none of Bluemoon's original data or music is included. Sound is permanently disabled in this build, and only the first road has been verified through its completion gate, so treat the other twenty-nine as untested.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard, which this build requires
Awareness that the full thirty-road campaign is unverified
howToOpen: Open the Open Skyways build on Decomp Games.
Press Enter to leave the intro, then choose Play and pick a road.
Accelerate and brake with the up and down arrows, steer with left and right, and press Space to jump.
games.statusNote: Clean-room engine reconstruction with its own thirty courses, hosted by Decomp Games. Audio is disabled.

games.name: SuperTuxKart (Wasm)
games.summary: The open-source kart racer, compiled to run in a browser tab.
games.whatItIs: SuperTuxKart is the long-running open-source kart racer, and this is an experimental WebAssembly port of it. The port's author reports that everything works except some rendering APIs and networking, so expect single-player racing rather than online play. It is the heaviest entry in this library: the low-quality texture set alone is a 120 MB download, the high set is 249 MB, and the game asks for roughly 500 MB of memory, which makes it a poor fit for a low-end machine or a slow connection.
whatYouNeed: A desktop browser with WebAssembly support
Bandwidth for a 120 MB or larger initial download
howToOpen: Open the SuperTuxKart Wasm page.
Choose a texture quality: low is 120 MB, medium 171 MB, high 249 MB.
Press Start Game and let the download finish before expecting a menu.
games.statusNote: Experimental WebAssembly port. Rendering APIs and networking are incomplete, and the initial download is 120 MB or more.

games.name: Stunts
games.altName: 4D Sports Driving, DOS build in browser
games.summary: The 1990 stunt-driving classic, running from its DOS build in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Stunts, released by Broderbund in 1990 and sold in Europe as 4D Sports Driving, is an early 3D driving game built around looping tracks, jumps and a track editor rather than straightforward circuit racing. It runs here from the DOS build through browser emulation, so the original executable and its deliberately slidey handling model are preserved. Mouse handling inside the DOS environment can be awkward, so fullscreen mode is worth trying if the pointer drifts.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard, plus a mouse for the menus
howToOpen: Open the Stunts page on DOS Zone.
Wait for the DOS bundle to load, then click the screen to capture input.
Choose a car and track from the menu, and switch to fullscreen if the pointer misbehaves.
games.statusNote: Runs the 1990 Broderbund DOS build through browser emulation. Free to play without registration.

games.name: Wacky Wheels
games.summary: Apogee's animal kart racer, running from its DOS build in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Wacky Wheels is Apogee's animal-themed kart racer, an answer to Super Mario Kart in which you collect hedgehogs and bombs and fire them at the other drivers. It runs here from the DOS build through a browser DOS environment, and it is notable for including a dedicated battle mode alongside the races, plus split-screen play in the original release. The build boots as version 1.1 and reports itself as the registered release, so the full character and course set is available rather than a cut-down demo.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard, plus a mouse for the menus
Patience with DOS-era menus and key mapping
howToOpen: Open the Wacky Wheels page on DOS Zone.
Click the screen to capture input.
Pick a character and course, then drive with the arrow keys.
games.statusNote: Runs the 1994 Apogee DOS build through browser emulation. The build boots as version 1.1 and reports itself as registered.

games.name: 1080° Snowboarding
games.summary: The N64 snowboarding game, rebuilt to run in a browser from the clean-room pipeline.
games.whatItIs: 1080° Snowboarding is Nintendo's 1998 N64 snowboarding game, split between downhill races and trick runs across six courses, with scoring that rewards both speed and style. This build runs the retail program through EmulatorJS with textures, images and audio regenerated by the clean-room pipeline, so it ships no original ROM, textures or audio. The regenerated art deliberately differs from the retail release.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard or gamepad, because the trick runs need more than two inputs
A tolerance for regenerated textures and a substitute soundtrack
howToOpen: Open the 1080° Snowboarding build on Decomp Games.
Tap or press a key once, since sound only starts after your first input.
Pick a course and a mode; touch controls are still being rolled out, so use a keyboard or pad.
games.statusNote: Clean-room browser build of the N64 original, hosted by Decomp Games. A race plays start to finish; assets are regenerated.

games.name: International Sensible Soccer
games.summary: The 1994 football classic, running from its DOS build in a browser.
games.whatItIs: International Sensible Soccer is Sensible Software's 1994 football game, played from a zoomed-out top-down view that keeps passing and through balls readable at speed. It is remembered for tight controls and pace rather than presentation, and it runs here from the DOS build through a browser DOS environment with no registration. Virtual controls are provided for touch devices, though a keyboard is the better way to play it.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard, or a gamepad if you prefer
Awareness that the DOS-era control scheme is not the modern default
howToOpen: Open the International Sensible Soccer page on DOS Zone.
Click the screen to capture input.
Pick a team and a match type from the menus, then check the key layout before kick-off.
games.statusNote: Runs the 1994 DOS build through browser emulation. Free to play without registration.

games.name: Open Digger
games.summary: The 1983 arcade maze-digger, rebuilt with new mazes and free assets.
games.whatItIs: Open Digger rebuilds Digger, the 1983 arcade game in which you tunnel through a maze collecting emeralds while dodging roaming enemies and dropping bags on their heads. This build pairs the Digger Remastered decompilation with eight independently designed mazes and a complete CC0 visual set, so it contains none of the original maps, graphics, fonts or tunes. Audio is disabled by design, and the deliberately geometric artwork looks nothing like the original.
whatYouNeed: Around 5 MB of bandwidth for the first load
howToOpen: Open the Open Digger build on Decomp Games.
Press Enter to start, then move and dig with the arrow keys.
Press F1 to fire and Space to pause; F10 exits the game.
games.statusNote: Clean-room decompilation with eight replacement mazes, hosted by Decomp Games. Audio is disabled by design.

games.name: Mortal Kombat
games.summary: The 1993 fighting game, running from its DOS build in a browser.
games.whatItIs: Mortal Kombat is the 1993 fighting game that made digitised actors and finishing moves famous, and it runs here from the DOS build through a browser DOS environment. The DOS release keeps the original roster and the two-player versus mode, and it is free to play on DOS Zone without registration. One thing to expect before you start: this build opens with the manual-based copy-protection check, the screen that asks for a word from a given page, paragraph, line and word of the printed booklet, so you need the manual or the answer before you reach the character select screen. Virtual controls are provided for touch devices, but a keyboard is the better way to learn the special moves.
whatYouNeed: A keyboard, since the special moves need two-handed input
The DOS manual, or the answer to the copy-protection word check
Patience with the DOS-era key mapping
howToOpen: Open the Mortal Kombat page on DOS Zone.
Let the DOS bundle load, then click the screen to capture input.
Clear the copy-protection screen by entering the word it asks for from the manual.
Read the control list before you start, then pick a fighter and a mode.
games.statusNote: Runs the 1993 DOS build through browser emulation. Free to play without registration, but the build opens with the manual-based copy-protection word check.
